specification:
Functional Description:
The `read` method reads bytes from a chunked stream into a provided `ByteBuffer` destination. It manages the reading of chunks, handles end-of-stream conditions, and invokes a finish listener when the last chunk is processed. The method interacts with a chunk reader to determine the remaining data to read and utilizes a buffer wrapper for memory management.

Args:
- `dst` (ByteBuffer): The destination buffer where read bytes will be stored
Returns:
int - The number of bytes read into the destination buffer. Returns -1 if the end of the stream is reached, 0 if no bytes are read, and a positive integer indicating the number of bytes successfully read.

Preconditions:
- The conduit must not already be closed when a read requiring data is attempted; the method explicitly throws when `closed` is true.
Postconditions:
- The contents of `dst` will be updated with bytes read from the stream.
- The state of the chunk reader will be updated to reflect the remaining chunks.
- If the last chunk is read, the finish listener will be invoked.
Invariants:
None
Exception:
- `ClosedChannelException`: Thrown when the conduit is closed, when the underlying stream ends before the current chunk is complete, or when reads are attempted after premature termination.
- A reached `IOException`, `RuntimeException`, or `Error` from chunk processing is recorded through `IoUtils.safeClose(closeable)` and then rethrown.

specification:
Functional Description:
The `encode` method encodes HTTP/2 headers into a specified `ByteBuffer` using the HPACK compression format. It manages overflow scenarios when the target buffer is insufficient, iterating through the headers and applying Huffman encoding as needed, while also handling dynamic table updates for previously seen headers.

Args:
- `headers` (HeaderMap): The collection of headers to encode
- `target` (ByteBuffer): The buffer where the encoded headers will be written
Returns:
State - The method returns an enumeration indicating the result of the encoding process. It can return:
- `State.COMPLETE` if all headers were successfully encoded.
- `State.OVERFLOW` if the target buffer was insufficient to hold the encoded headers, indicating that some data has been written to an overflow buffer.

Preconditions:
- During continuation after a previous `OVERFLOW`, `headers` must be the same object stored in `currentHeaders`.
Postconditions:
- The `target` buffer will contain the encoded headers if the method completes successfully.
- If the method returns `State.OVERFLOW`, the `overflowData` field will contain the remaining data that could not fit into the `target` buffer, and `overflowPos` will indicate the position in the overflow data.
Invariants:
None
Exception:
- `IllegalStateException`: Thrown when continuation is attempted with a different `HeaderMap` instance.

name: handle
specification:
Functional Description:
The `handle` method processes a `ByteBuffer` containing HTTP/2 frame data, parsing the frame header and delegating to specific frame parsers based on the frame type. It manages state transitions and error handling for various frame types, ensuring compliance with the HTTP/2 protocol.

Args:

Returns:
- boolean: Returns `true` if the parsing of the current frame is finished, otherwise returns `false`. The return value indicates whether the parser has completed processing the frame based on the input data.

None
Postconditions:
- The state of the `parser` field is updated to reflect the current frame parser based on the frame type. If the frame is a continuation frame, the `continuationParser` may be set or cleared based on the flags. The method may also throw exceptions for protocol errors or incorrect frame sizes.
Invariants:
None
Exception:
- `ConnectionErrorException`: Thrown by explicit HTTP/2 protocol and frame-size checks for invalid stream IDs, lengths, or continuation sequencing.
- The exception returned by `http2ContinuationFrameNotExpected()` is thrown for an unexpected or mismatched continuation frame.

specification:
Functional Description:
The `create` method constructs an `AnnotatedEndpointFactory` instance based on the provided WebSocket endpoint class, an encoding factory, and a set of paths. It inspects the methods of the endpoint class for specific WebSocket annotations (`@OnOpen`, `@OnClose`, `@OnError`, `@OnMessage`) and binds them to corresponding `BoundMethod` instances, ensuring that no more than one method is annotated with the same annotation type.

Args:
- `endpointClass` (Class<?>): The class representing the WebSocket endpoint
- `encodingFactory` (EncodingFactory): An instance responsible for encoding and decoding messages
- `paths` (Set<String>): A set of path strings that may be used for binding path parameters
Returns:
AnnotatedEndpointFactory - Returns a new instance of `AnnotatedEndpointFactory` that encapsulates the provided endpoint class and its associated bound methods. The returned factory reflects the methods annotated with WebSocket annotations found in the input class.

Preconditions:
- No annotation category may resolve to more than one bound method, and each `@OnMessage` method must expose a supported message parameter.
Postconditions:
- A new `AnnotatedEndpointFactory` is created and returned, encapsulating the endpoint class and its bound methods.
- The internal state of the factory reflects the methods found in the endpoint class, including any associated path parameters.
Invariants:
None
Exception:
- `DeploymentException`: Thrown when more than one method is found for an annotation category or when an `@OnMessage` method has no supported message parameter.
